reason: Both opened with identical, correct safety advice (unplug, never remove the casing) and both ended by over-escalating to an engineer instead of recommending the justified DIY fix of replacing the waveguide cover and cleaning the cavity. Conversation 1's final turn is a generic smoke/burning-smell template that ignores everything the homeowner reported, offering no diagnosis, no part name and no explanation. Conversation 2 correctly identifies the 'cardboard-like panel' as the waveguide cover, explains that the burnt spot is the arcing source, and notes replacement is usually simple, giving the homeowner a genuine understanding of the fault even though it then hedges with an unsupported magnetron-damage speculation and defers to Panasonic rather than pointing them to the model-specific part.
